caption: Send: a master clock sent to two places without a wire - the wave's phase and the palette's scroll
why: A value used all over a big graph - the beat, the clock, a master speed - means wires from one node crossing everything to reach the others. Send and Receive carry it without a wire: whatever feeds a Send named clock comes out of every Receive named clock, wherever they sit.
Its neighbours: Knot routes a wire neatly; sub-graphs hide wiring inside a node; Send and Receive remove the wire. Send colour and Receive colour do the same for colours.
steps: **name** is clock: every Receive named clock gives that value.
Two Receives named clock feed the **Wave**'s phase and the palette's scroll (through an **Add** with **Coords** `u`) - two wires that never have to be drawn across the graph.
When the graph compiles each Receive is joined to the Send, and both nodes vanish: they cost nothing.

try.label: Another name
try.text: name tick: the Receives are still called clock, so they no longer find a Send - each Receive says so on the node, and the build stops until the names agree.
